Our Founding Story – From the First Code to the Vision of a Digital Future

Every startup begins with an idea, a challenge, and, above all, people who have the courage to take new paths. At Kydo, Adrian, Luca, and Roy stand behind the vision of creating an intuitive, flexible, and efficient document management system. In this article, you'll learn how the three founders embarked on their entrepreneurial journey, the challenges they had to overcome, and what drives them.

The three founders bring together different but complementary backgrounds: Adrian gained his first experience as a developer at Infopro and was part of a newly formed dev team from the very beginning, which later became the independent company Eutima – a formative time in which he learned how to build something from scratch.

Luca started at Infopro AG right after graduation, where he contributed to the founding of Eutima in an innovation-driven environment. This experience reinforced his desire to help shape his own company.

Roy began with a commercial apprenticeship but discovered his passion for IT in the call center industry. A second apprenticeship as an application developer and a part-time degree program optimally prepared him for the technical challenges of entrepreneurship.

The Birth of Kydo: A Vision Becomes Reality

The idea for Kydo emerged from practical experience. Florian, a mutual colleague, noticed in various projects that existing document management systems were often expensive, complicated, and inflexible. This led the team to develop a better solution: software that offers companies an efficient, cost-effective, and user-friendly alternative.

A key moment was the collaboration with the first client, Alluvia AG. The challenge was to create a flexible and versatile solution tailored precisely to their needs. Later, a partnership with PINIT AG followed, leading to a specialized version of Kydo for the gastronomy industry.

Challenges and Doubts: What Keeps the Team Together

One of the biggest challenges in the early phase was balancing product development with financial stability. Adrian puts it succinctly: "Of course, you want to push the product as far as possible, but at the same time, you must remain financially viable." The founders had to learn to set priorities consciously and make pragmatic decisions.

The transition from employee to entrepreneur was also a significant step for Luca: "We are engineers and software developers, but running a company meant learning entirely new entrepreneurial skills." The support from the Bigint Group helped the team navigate this new role and focus on technological development.

The Philosophy Behind Kydo

The name "Kydo" stands for "Keep Your Data Organized" – and that is precisely the company's core philosophy. Roy emphasizes: "We want to provide businesses with a simple and cost-effective way to structure and organize their documents centrally."

But it's not just about technology. Luca highlights that people are at the center of Kydo: "We want to reverse the trend where customers are left alone with complicated systems. Our goal is to offer intuitive solutions with real support."

Looking Ahead: Where Will Kydo Be in Five Years?

The vision of the three founders is clear: Kydo aims to establish itself as the standard for digital document management in Switzerland and beyond. Luca puts it ambitiously: "We want Kydo to become for digital document management what the Adobe Suite is for image and video editing."

Adrian hopes that in five years, hundreds of companies will be using Kydo to simplify their daily work. At the same time, Roy emphasizes that a crucial milestone is the product's financial independence: "Our goal is to develop Kydo to the point where it fully sustains itself, allowing us to focus entirely on its further development."

Tips for Other Founders

Every startup experiences ups and downs, but the three founders agree: perseverance pays off. Adrian advises: "You shouldn't get lost in the daily grind but always remind yourself why you took this step."

Luca adds: "Be the change you want to see in the world. Don't wait for others to take the initiative." Roy sees passion as the key factor: "Believe in your product and be willing to give more than just the classic 9-to-5 workday."

Conclusion: One Team, One Vision, One Mission

Kydo is more than just software – it is the result of hard work, perseverance, and a shared vision. The founders have shown that it is worth fighting for an idea and taking new paths. And for businesses looking to advance digitally, Kydo is the perfect solution.
